method_notes:
WHAT WAS FETCHED (all UK storefront 'gb', fetched 2026-10-10). App IDs came from the iTunes Search API (https://itunes.apple.com/search?term=&entity=software&country=gb&limit=5); trackName and sellerName were checked for each. Revolut — Mobile Finance (Revolut Ltd) id 932493382, https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/revolut-mobile-finance/id932493382. Monzo Bank - Mobile Banking (Monzo Bank Limited) id 1052238659, https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/monzo-bank-mobile-banking/id1052238659. Plum: Smart Saving & Investing (Plum Fintech Limited) id 1456139507, https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/plum-smart-saving-investing/id1456139507. Chip – Savings and Investments (Chip Financial Ltd) id 1141297472, https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/chip-savings-and-investments/id1141297472. Moneybox - Save and Invest (Digital Moneybox Limited) id 1049797239, https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/moneybox-save-and-invest/id1049797239. Store averages from the API: Revolut 4.86 (1,088,013 ratings), Monzo 4.86 (360,674), Plum 4.68 (70,939), Chip 4.66 (39,466), Moneybox 4.75 (79,097). Minimum iOS: Monzo 17.0, Chip 17.0, Plum 16.6, Moneybox 16.0, Revolut 15.0. Reviews came from Apple's RSS feed, https://itunes.apple.com/gb/rss/customerreviews/page=<1..10>/id=/sortby=mostrecent/json. Every page returned 50 entries, so each app reached the feed's 500-review cap. No app failed, so there was no web fallback, and every complaint is data_basis app_store_rss_counted. Date windows of the most-recent samples: Revolut 2026-10-05 to 10-08 (3 days), Monzo 2026-07-17 to 10-08, Plum 2025-01-09 to 2026-10-05, Chip 2023-02-12 to 2026-09-29, Moneybox 2023-08-19 to 2026-10-05. SUPPLEMENT (deviation from plan, flagged). Revolut's 500 most-recent reviews held only 9 one- or two-star reviews, and 4 of those were praise left with the wrong star rating. I therefore also pulled sortby=mosthelpful (10 pages each) for Revolut and Monzo. I kept reviews dated 2023-01-01 or later and dropped any already in the recent sample: Revolut +200 reviews (70 one- or two-star), Monzo +333 (145 one- or two-star). Most-helpful sorting favours long, dramatic reviews, so those counts are reported split recent/supplement. CODING. I read every one- and two-star review: Revolut 9+70, Monzo 84+145, Plum 320, Chip 248, Moneybox 208, total 1,084. I also skimmed the three-star reviews. I wrote a codebook of 21 themes after the first ~60 reviews per app, then implemented it as regex rules in scripts/classify.js. Each review gets at most 2 themes (most pattern hits, then a priority order). Short positive texts are flagged MISRATED and get no theme. Rules were refined over 4 passes. Fixes included straight versus curly apostrophes, 'challenger' falsely matching 'challenge', 'moved house', closures 'without explanation' falsely counted as unwanted debits, and 'funds have been held'. Accuracy check on two random samples. Before the refinements, 37 of 45 reviews had the right primary theme. After them, 36 of 40 did. Small themes, such as Revolut fees and unwanted debits, are noisier. Theme counts per app add up to more than the number of reviews because each review can carry 2 themes. Praise was measured with keyword buckets over 4- and 5-star reviews (scripts/praise.js), plus a cross-rating search for locking, sounds, widgets and personalisation. CAVEATS. Written RSS reviews are far more negative than the store averages; for example, Plum's sample is 54% one-star against a 4.68 average. Treat the shares as shares of complaints, not of all users. Feature facts come from App Store descriptions (URLs above) and these web sources: - https://help.revolut.com/en-US/help/app-features/vaults/how-do-spare-change-round-ups-work/ (read via search result; direct fetch returned 403) - https://www.revolut.com/news/revolut_launches_group_vaults_transforming_the_way_friends_and_family_save/ - https://monzo.com/blog/take-on-the-spare-change-saving-challenge (Jan 2020) - https://monzo.com/legal/savings-challenge/terms-and-conditions (v1.1, 9 Jan 2026) - https://monzo.com/blog/2018/07/03/custom-app-icons - https://community.monzo.com/t/we-re-launching-grow-tab-sign-up-for-early-access/190853 - https://help.withplum.com/en/articles/11721138-new-subscriptions-comparison-table - https://blog.withplum.com/1p-challenge/ - https://withplum.com/ - https://www.getchip.uk/ - https://becleverwithyourcash.com/chip-app-autosave/ (third party) - https://www.moneyboxapp.com/support/deposits-and-withdrawals/round-ups/how-do-round-ups-work (via search result) - https://moneyboxapp.com/support/deposits-and-withdrawals/depositing/how-can-i-pay-in (via search result) Features tagged [reviews] are user-reported only. cross_app_themes: 1. Losing access to your own money is the top source of anger in every app. Frozen or closed accounts make up 18–19% of one- and two-star reviews at Monzo and Revolut. Slow, failed or 'missing' withdrawals and transfers make up 18–21% at Plum, Chip and Moneybox. Vaultwise deliberately restricts access, so this is its biggest risk: users already hate opaque release. Data: theme-counts.json.

2. Support that hides behind bots is the most-cited problem at Revolut (41%), Monzo (28%) and Plum (23%), and it is 14–18% at Chip and Moneybox. The complaints are about not having a human with case memory and an ETA, not about AI as such.

3. Reliability and device cut-offs. Chip had a crash-on-launch release (34 reviews in 6 days, Apr 2024). Monzo's iOS 17 minimum produced 12 one- and two-star reviews in Jul–Sep 2026 (minOS 17.0 per the iTunes API). Lockouts compound point 1.

4. Redesigns that hide savings. Monzo's Grow tab moved Pots (23 coded complaints; 9 recent 1–3★ mentions). Moneybox and Plum redesigns buried round-ups and shrank pocket totals. Users want their pots one tap away and stable.

5. Paywalling the savings mechanics backfires. Plum moved pocket interest to the £14.99 Max tier in Sept 2026 (11 reviews in ~6 weeks, users switching to Monzo). Challenges are on paid tiers at Plum, and Monzo's 1p challenge needs a paid plan. Chip charges 45p per autosave.

6. Consent and control over automated pulls. Unexpected 'welcome deposits', deposits continuing after cancelling, overdrafts, and an autosave the user never enabled: 19 at Plum, 6 at Moneybox, 5 at Chip.

7. Demand for commitment devices is real (inferred from praise). Monzo users praise locking pots against temptation. Chip users mourn the 90-day account as help for impulsive spenders. Moneybox users like notice accounts that stop them dipping in. The same users hate it when a legitimate release needs a chat with an agent (Moneybox LISA).
8. Pay directly from a pot or vault is requested unprompted (Revolut 2025-03-07 and 2026-10-05; Monzo 2025-05-25). This validates Pay with Vaultwise.

9. Sensory identity matters to users. Monzo's Oct 2026 sound change drew 7 reviews across all star ratings in 6 days, asking to restore it or let them choose. A Revolut user says the transfer sound made every transaction feel exciting. Monzo's paycheck-drag animation and pot images are praised.

10. Personalisation and glanceable surfaces are wanted: home-screen widgets (6 requests or complaints across Monzo, Plum and Moneybox), dark mode (Plum, 2), app icons, wallpapers, themes and card colours (Monzo, Revolut).

11. Trust signals. Chip users question deposit protection and the lack of a password. Plum's SMS-plus-PIN login is called weak. Missing sort codes or account numbers make savings apps feel 'not a real bank' (Chip, Moneybox).

12. Onboarding failures (12–17% at Monzo, Revolut, Chip and Moneybox): camera ID failures, loops, unexplained refusals. Teenagers try to sign up and are rejected without guidance (Monzo, Moneybox, Plum).
13. Fraud handling (Revolut 15%, Monzo 9%). Victims describe fast automated rejections. Purpose locks could double as scam protection (inference).

opportunities.beats_competitors_because: Competitors show generic 'pending' or 'the team is working on it' with no ETA (Plum, Chip, Revolut, Monzo). Vaultwise holds money by design, so a transparent release is the trust contract.
opportunities.complaint_evidence: Withdraw/stuck money: Plum 66 (20.6%), Chip 45 (18.1%), Moneybox 40 (19.2%), Monzo 30, Revolut 13. Frozen with no timeline: Monzo 41, Revolut 15.

opportunities.beats_competitors_because: Plum's 'welcome deposit' and post-cancel pulls, Chip's autosave the user never switched on, and Moneybox's weekly-only collections and LISA default payments are the dark patterns users name.
opportunities.complaint_evidence: Unwanted debits: Plum 19, Moneybox 6, Chip 5. Moneybox rigid cadence 7. Plum round-ups not working (several reviews).

opportunities.idea: Keep core savings mechanics free: round-ups, challenges and streaks, and interest or yield on every vault. One plain fee page, and a notice before any change.
opportunities.beats_competitors_because: Plum's Sept 2026 move of pocket interest to Max (£14.99) is sending users to Monzo. Challenges are paywalled at Plum and Monzo. Chip charges 45p per autosave.
opportunities.complaint_evidence: Plum savings tools 35 (11 on the interest-paywall change since Aug 2026), Plum fees 28. Chip fee and debit complaints 10. Monzo challenge terms require a paid plan.

opportunities.beats_competitors_because: Users value locks and notice accounts (Monzo, Chip, Moneybox) but hate the Moneybox LISA 'message an agent to withdraw' flow and 25% penalty surprises. Chip removed its 90-day account that helped impulsive spenders.
